first.rationale:
The two declining metrics this quarter are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), which points directly at the onboarding/activation funnel rather than at pricing. Reacting to the competitor's entry pricing with promotional_pricing (memory_73) would defend a symptom, likely compress margin, and pull in exactly the price-sensitive accounts least likely to become sustainable qualified revenue; referral_incentive and enterprise_sales_assist address segments that are not currently degrading. So simplify_onboarding is the best-leveraged single slot, with activation_messaging as the fallback if verification undercuts it.

I am spending the one verification pull on memory_31 rather than memory_86 because memory_31 is the most load-bearing and the most quietly dangerous. It is the oldest record (day 12), and its stated mechanism — cutting required fields at signup — is precisely the kind of change that lifts a proxy metric (first-week activation) while degrading the thing we actually care about. Fewer required fields means less qualification data, weaker routing and scoring, and potentially a flood of low-intent signups that inflate activation counts while reducing qualified revenue. The memory as consolidated says nothing about whether revenue quality or downstream conversion was ever measured, or over what horizon 'durable' was assessed. memory_86 is more recent and its framing (time-to-value) is closer to real value, so it is the safer of the two to leave unverified.

I want to see from the archive: what the original outcome metric actually was, whether any revenue-quality or lead-quality metric was tracked, the follow-up window, and the sample. If it turns out the lift was measured only on signup-to-activation counts with no qualified-revenue check, I will treat the memory as evidence about a proxy and not about the objective, and shift the slot to activation_messaging (memory_91), which improves engagement for accounts that have already self-selected in and therefore carries much less adverse-selection risk.

Running this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout: the confounded environment (a competitor actively poaching SMB accounts) means any funnel movement this quarter is hard to attribute, and a broad rollout would bake an unverified proxy-metric assumption into the whole self-serve funnel. Guardrails should include downstream qualified-lead rate and paid-conversion, not just completion and activation, with a rollback trigger if lead quality drops even while activation rises.

final.rationale:
The archive substantially supports memory_31 but also confirms the dilution pattern I was worried about, so I proceed with simplify_onboarding while keeping the guardrails.

What the record shows: signup +15%, activation +9%, qualified revenue +4%, 30-day retention -1%. Critically, someone did measure qualified revenue, and it moved positively — so this is not a pure proxy-metric artifact and the memory is honestly consolidated. But the gradient is telling: the effect decays monotonically as you move from the shallow metric to the one we actually care about (15 -> 9 -> 4). That is the signature of adverse selection — cutting required fields brings in a meaningful tail of lower-intent signups that register as activations but never become qualified revenue. The headline 'durable lift in first-week activation' overstates what this buys us against the stated objective by roughly a factor of three. The -1% retention is small but points the same direction and was measured only to 30 days, so I cannot rule out further decay on a longer horizon.

Why still this action: the two metrics actually degrading this quarter are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which is exactly the funnel this intervention addresses, and it is corroborated by memory_86 (time-to-value, a value-linked mechanism) and memory_91. The alternatives are worse fits — promotional_pricing (memory_73) would chase the competitor into a margin war and preferentially recruit the least sustainable accounts; referral_incentive and enterprise_sales_assist target segments that are not the source of the decline.

Scope and guardrails: SMB self-serve only, since the record explicitly says the result did not replicate on other segments — I will not generalize it to enterprise, where memory_44 says sales-assisted flows win and where stripping qualification fields would actively damage routing. Small guarded test rather than broad rollout for two reasons: the competitor's SMB pricing push is an active confound that will contaminate attribution on any funnel metric this quarter, and a broad rollout would permanently bake the field reduction into the funnel before we know whether the +4% survives past 30 days.

Primary success metric is qualified revenue per signup, not activation count or completion rate — if activation rises while qualified-revenue-per-signup falls, that is a failure and triggers rollback. Secondary guardrails: downstream paid-conversion rate, lead-quality/routing accuracy, and retention tracked past 30 days. I will also preserve the specific fields that feed qualification and routing rather than cutting required fields indiscriminately, which should let us keep most of the time-to-value gain while limiting the low-intent tail. Residual uncertainty: exp_31 is 64 days old and predates the current competitive environment, so the effect size may not transfer.
